population.definition: Resident population of Kampala Capital City per the UBOS 2024 National Population and Housing Census, as reported by EBSCO. The UBOS report itself could not be opened, so the exact census definition (de facto vs usual residents) is unverified.

source.title: Kampala, Uganda
source.author: Beverly Ballaro
source.quote: Kampala Capital City had a resident population of 1,797,722.

facts.claim: The Kampala site was where the Buganda king held his royal court; Lugard's company made it its headquarters in 1890.

source.title: Kampala, Uganda
source.author: Beverly Ballaro
source.quote: had traditionally served as the place where the king of the Buganda Kingdom held his royal court.

facts.claim: Captain Lugard set up a fortified camp at Old Kampala in 1890, without the Kabaka's permission.

source.title: Kampala city's troubles
source.author: Joseph Bossa
source.quote: established a camp at Old Kampala in 1890 and proceeded to fortify it.

facts.claim: Mengo, not Kampala, was the official capital of Buganda; the kibuga is the settlement around the Kabaka's palace.

source.title: Kampala city's troubles
source.author: Joseph Bossa
source.quote: Kibuga can mean 'town', the 'capital', or the settlement surrounding the palace (lubiri) of the Kabaka.

facts.claim: The British moved their administration to Entebbe in 1894; Kampala became national capital again at independence in 1962.

source.title: Kampala, Uganda
source.author: Beverly Ballaro
source.quote: In 1894, the British colonial authorities transferred their administrative structure to the city of Entebbe.

facts.claim: Kampala is credited with over 60 percent of Uganda's GDP and 80 percent of industrial output.

source.title: Kampala, Uganda
source.author: Beverly Ballaro
source.quote: reportedly contributing over 60 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) and producing 80 percent of industrial output

places.name: Nakasero Market
places.what: A produce market in central Kampala, opened in 1927 during the colonial period. It now has about 10,000 vendors, traders and service providers.

places.name: Owino Market (St Balikuddembe Market)
places.what: A large public market in Kampala, one of 16 run by KCCA. It was built at Nakivubo in 1971.

source.title: Court settles battle for soul of Owino market
source.author: Busein Samilu
source.quote: St Balikuddembe market was constructed at Nakivubo in 1971 covering about 8.5 acres of land.

places.name: Uganda Museum
places.what: Uganda's museum, founded in 1908 with exhibits on culture, archaeology, history, science and natural history. It moved several times before reaching Kitante.

places.name: Namirembe Cathedral

places.name: Namugongo Martyrs Shrine
places.what: Catholic shrine in Namugongo, just outside Kampala, honouring Christians killed on the orders of King Mwanga. Pilgrims gather each 3 June.
